      Type (max v w)

      The supplement formulation used in BGRS 3.4. The image of every Hom map has a chosen linear complement, and those complements form a subfunctor of the target Hom bifunctor. This is precisely the concrete datum called a cleavage in the source.

                                          Generic cleaving transfer from split extension objects. Each extension may be decomposable. Finite-dimensionality and a displayed finite indecomposable decomposition produce one target lift for each source object; the preceding theorem then removes repetitions.
